notes.meaning: Nebuchadnezzar had troubling dreams during his second year as sole ruler of Babylon. Even though the word is plural, he had one single dream that contained many parts. God sent this dream and shook the king's heart so deeply that he could not sleep. If we could see into the anxious hearts of great rulers, we would often pity them rather than envy them.

The king called together every group of court advisers to explain his dream. These included scholars, astrologers who studied the stars, enchanters, and sorcerers. God stirred up the king so that he could find no rest until the meaning of the vision was made plain.

Nebuchadnezzar told the wise men that his mind was deeply troubled to understand what he had seen. He had awakened in great alarm, feeling the weight of a divine message that he could not fully grasp. Even in the middle of worldly security, God can instantly shake the peace of the mightiest earthly kings.

The court astrologers greeted the king with a polite wish for long life and asked him to describe the dream. Starting at this verse, the book shifts from Hebrew to Aramaic, the common language of the Babylonian world. This change shows that the message now concerns the rise and fall of world powers.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some critical scholars argue that using the word 'Chaldeans' for astrologers is a historical mistake that points to a second-century BC date for the book.

notes.meaning: The king demanded that they tell him both the dream and what it meant, or else they would be torn to pieces and their homes turned into ruins. Nebuchadnezzar either had forgotten the dream or refused to share it as a strict test of their claims. This harsh threat shows the brutal anger of an unchecked ruler, which God used to expose the empty boasting of Babylon's wise men.

Alongside his threats, the king offered rich gifts, high honor, and lavish rewards if they could reveal both the dream and its meaning. Pagan advisers often told fortunes for money, so Nebuchadnezzar tried to tempt them with great wealth. His eagerness shows how desperate he was to unlock the mystery.

The wise men repeated their request for the king to recount his dream first. They were forced to admit that their methods could only offer an interpretation for a story already told to them. When pushed to the limit, human cleverness cannot produce answers it does not have.

The king saw right through their stalling and accused them of trying to buy time. He knew they were delaying because they saw his decree was firm and they were helpless to answer. When people make false claims about spiritual power, a real crisis quickly exposes them.

Nebuchadnezzar warned that only one death sentence stood against them if they failed to reveal the dream. He accused them of conspiring to tell lies and stalling until his mood softened or the crisis passed. By demanding the dream itself, the king set up a test to prove whether their interpretation could really be trusted.

The astrologers admitted that no person on earth could ever do what the king was asking. They pointed out that no great monarch had ever placed such an impossible demand on any magician or priest. By their own confession, pagan arts are powerless to discover secrets that belong only to God.

The wise men insisted that only the gods could reveal such a secret, and those gods do not live among mortal men. In their pagan view, the highest gods remained distant and completely cut off from human beings. They did not know the true God, who later drew near and entered our world to dwell with us.

The king flew into a wild fury at their answer and commanded that all the wise men in Babylon be destroyed. While the king's order was cruel and tyrannical, God used it justly to expose men who had made a living by pretending to have divine knowledge. When worldly wisdom fails, anger often takes over.

The death decree was published, and the guards began rounding up the wise men, including Daniel and his three friends. The young Hebrews had not been called into the king's original meeting, likely because of their youth or novitiate status. Yet by this decree, innocent men were condemned right alongside the deceivers.

When Arioch, the commander of the executioners, arrived to carry out the sentence, Daniel responded with calm wisdom and good judgment. Instead of panicking or fighting back, he spoke with gentle self-control. Sudden crises reveal a person's faith and trust in God.

Daniel asked Arioch why the king's decree had been issued with such harsh and sudden haste. He had been completely unaware of the king's dream and the confrontation with the other wise men until this moment. Arioch then laid out the entire crisis for him.

Daniel went and asked the king for a delay, promising that he would provide the interpretation. Unlike the Chaldeans, who only asked to hear the dream, Daniel stepped forward trusting that God would give him the answer. Asking for time was an act of faith to seek the Lord, not a trick to stall.

Daniel went back to his quarters and shared the whole crisis with his three companions, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. He sought time from the king specifically so he and his friends could seek the Lord together. It is a great blessing to have trusted friends who share the same faith in moments of danger.

Daniel urged his friends to plead for mercy from the God of heaven so they would not be killed with the rest of Babylon's wise men. They based their request entirely on God's free kindness, not on their own goodness or merit. When lives are on the line, believers are called to pray together with earnest faith.

God answered their united prayers and revealed the secret dream to Daniel during a night vision. Without waiting to see the king's reaction, Daniel immediately stopped to praise and bless the God of heaven. When God gives an answer, our very first duty is to offer Him heartfelt thanks.

Daniel began his song of praise by blessing God's name forever because wisdom and power belong entirely to Him. While human beings often have power without wisdom or wisdom without power, both exist perfectly together in the Lord. God deserves unending praise for who He is and what He does.

God governs history by changing periods and eras, taking down kings and raising up new ones according to His own plan. Daniel's words give an early hint that the dream itself was about the rise and fall of world kingdoms. Human rulers hold power only because the sovereign God places them there.

The Lord uncovers the deepest secrets because He sees perfectly into the dark, and pure light lives with Him. Human minds are limited and blind to the future, but nothing is hidden from God's sight. He alone can share hidden truth through His prophets.

Daniel gave thanks to the God of his fathers, who had shown covenant faithfulness to him as an exile in Babylon. He credited the prayers of his companions by saying God made the answer known to 'us.' True humility leads God's servants to share the credit with their praying friends and give all glory to the Lord.

With the secret revealed, Daniel went to Arioch and told him to stop the execution of Babylon's wise men. He offered to be brought before the king to explain the interpretation. Even though the pagan wise men practiced deceitful arts, Daniel acted with kindness and fairness by stepping in to save their lives.
